title: Injury Woes: Sinner and Draper Withdraw from US Open, Alcaraz Returns
summary:
The US Open has lost two of its biggest stars before a single ball is hit. World number one Jannik Sinner and Britain's Jack Draper have both pulled out of the upcoming tournament due to injuries, dealing a blow to the men's draw.

Sinner, who has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon in July, is dealing with a knee problem. The 25-year-old Italian announced his withdrawal a day after his great rival Carlos Alcaraz confirmed he would compete at Flushing Meadows following a four-month absence with a wrist injury. "Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year," Sinner said. "I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart."

Draper, who lost to Sinner in the 2024 US Open semi-finals, has withdrawn because of the long-term arm injury that has stalled his progress. The former British number one was ranked inside the world's top five when he suffered bone bruising in his left serving arm. He has played just 16 matches in the past 12 months and missed all four Grand Slam tournaments this year.

The withdrawals mean Sinner and Alcaraz have not both been present at the past three Grand Slams. Their rivalry, which produced a clean sweep of Grand Slam titles in 2024 and 2025, has been unable to reach the same heights. Fans will now look to Alcaraz and other contenders to fill the void.
why_it_matters: Star withdrawals reshape entire tournaments: they change the likely champion, affect fan excitement and media attention, and show how fragile elite athletes' careers are under the physical load of modern tennis.

background_read: The US Open is one of tennis's four Grand Slam tournaments and is played each year at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows, a neighborhood in Queens, New York.

Jannik Sinner (Italy's world number one) and Carlos Alcaraz (a Spanish star and Sinner's biggest rival) have formed the defining rivalry of the current men's game, trading Grand Slam titles and the top ranking in recent seasons.
Jack Draper (a British left-hander who reached the 2024 US Open semi-finals) has spent much of the past year trying to recover from an arm injury that has kept him out of the sport's biggest events.
When top seeds like Sinner and Draper withdraw, the draw loses its expected star power, and younger or lower-ranked players suddenly have a clearer path to the later rounds.

Modern men's tennis has turned injury management into a central part of careers; hard courts, long seasons, and the serving motion put enormous strain on knees and shoulders, so short-term withdrawals are often made to protect long-term health.

perspectives.description: With Sinner and Draper out, lower-ranked players get a clearer draw and a rare chance to reach the second week or beyond. Underdog breakthroughs can refresh a tournament and create new storylines.

Star withdrawals weaken the event's commercial appeal and disappoint fans who bought tickets or tuned in to see the biggest names. TV audiences and media narratives often lose energy when the expected stars are absent.

The withdrawals highlight how hard courts, long seasons, and repetitive serving motion strain knees, shoulders, and arms. Players and teams now weigh short-term tournament points against long-term career health.
Alcaraz's return could help carry the US Open and set up a new phase of the rivalry if Sinner recovers. Draper faces a deeper question about whether his arm can withstand a full, healthy season.
